findings.summary: Sample check trace for R3 maps only to AT3, but AT3 does not validate the stated CommonMark-compliance aspect of R3; AT4 is the acceptance test that exercises Markdown structure/formatting and should be included in the R3 trace (or R3 should be split/clarified).

evidence.note: R3 includes an explicit CommonMark-compliant parsing requirement.
evidence.quote: The system MUST parse each discovered Markdown file using at least CommonMark-compliant syntax and generate a corresponding HTML page...

evidence.note: Deterministic sample check for R3 maps only to AT3.
AT3 verifies one-to-one page generation and exclusions, not CommonMark compliance.
evidence.quote: Count generated HTML note pages and verify a one-to-one mapping for non-excluded files.

evidence.note: AT4 is the acceptance test that actually checks Markdown element rendering fidelity, which is closer to exercising CommonMark behavior.
evidence.quote: Create a fixture Markdown file containing headings (H1/H2), ordered and unordered lists, bold/italic emphasis, links, images, and fenced code blocks...

findings.summary: Deterministic sample checks for R1–R3 list milestone M2 as covering these requirements, but M2 is scoped to tags (R11–R13) and does not introduce new deliverables for R1–R3; this appears to be trace noise/redundancy.

evidence.note: All three sample checks list milestones ["M1","M2"] for R1–R3.
M2 deliverables/exit criteria are about tags and acceptance tests AT11–AT13 (R11–R13), not R1–R3.
evidence.quote: Tags: extraction + normalization + tags index/per-tag pages + tag navigation
